gen.title: Checking rules for single gene inheritance

cards.stem: Which transmission rule characterizes X-linked inheritance?
options: fathers cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons
a variant can only be passed from father to son
only females can pass on mitochondrial variants to their children
cards.quote: A characteristic of X-linked inheritance is that fathers cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons (no male-to-male transmission).

cards.stem: How many altered copies are needed to be affected by an autosomal dominant disorder?
options: One altered copy of the gene in each cell is sufficient
variants occur in both copies of the gene in each cell
a variant can only be passed from father to son
cards.quote: One altered copy of the gene in each cell is sufficient for a person to be affected by an autosomal dominant disorder.

cards.stem: What defines autosomal recessive inheritance at the gene copy level?
options: variants occur in both copies of the gene in each cell
One altered copy of the gene in each cell is sufficient
only females can pass on mitochondrial variants to their children
cards.quote: In autosomal recessive inheritance, variants occur in both copies of the gene in each cell.

cards.stem: Who can transmit mitochondrial variants to children?
options: only females can pass on mitochondrial variants to their children
fathers cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons
a variant can only be passed from father to son
cards.quote: Because only egg cells contribute mitochondria to the developing embryo, only females can pass on mitochondrial variants to their children.
